strengths: Competing with switching comparators without knowing the switch budget is a well-motivated problem with an identifiable audience in online learning and bandit theory.

The master–base decomposition clearly exposes the cost of importance-weighted estimation. Lemma 3.3 provides useful analysis connecting adaptive base learning rates to square-root dependence on the reciprocal-probability threshold.

The manuscript provides explicit algorithm descriptions, proof sketches, and detailed appendix derivations. Its theoretical scope is appropriate; experiments or state-of-the-art performance are not prerequisites for acceptance.
weaknesses: Necessary: Theorem 3.2’s claimed dependence on K is not established by the stated tuning. Algorithm 2 sets η = √(H/T), so the negative term in (14) becomes −E[ρ_T(h†)]√T/(40√H log T). Equations (15) and (49) instead insert an additional √K. Even granting Lemma A.4, maximizing the correctly substituted bound over ρ gives Õ(SK√T), rather than the claimed Õ(S√(KT)). The algorithm, proof, and headline claims must be reconciled, or the theorem weakened. This is a polynomial discrepancy, not a hidden logarithmic factor.

Necessary: The proof of Lemma A.4 does not justify its central negative correction. It defines G as negative entropy on page 18, despite Algorithm 2 using a log barrier, and subsequently invokes log-barrier identities. Moreover, (46) is false as written: with all losses zero, learning rates never increase, so its left side is zero while its right side is strictly negative because ρ_T(h†) = 2H. The claimed correction also depends on the comparator’s mass at h† and cannot be asserted uniformly over arbitrary p before maximizing. A corrected proof should use the appropriate clipped comparator, handle the case without threshold updates, and consistently use the stated regularizer.

Necessary: Algorithm 1 is not defined throughout the stated parameter range. Its clipped simplex is nonempty only when Hα ≤ 1, equivalent to T ≥ KH^(3/2) for the prescribed α. No such restriction or fallback is supplied. Specify feasible parameters and establish the guarantee for the remaining regimes.

Optional positioning improvement: Include an S-independent fixed-rate baseline. A single clipped-entropy OMD instance with learning rate 1/√(KT) already yields Õ(S√(KT)) through the same interval analysis. Comparing against it would clarify the additional contribution of the ρ-dependent guarantee; outperforming it is not itself an acceptance requirement.

Optional implementation improvement: Give update formulas or solver details that match Algorithm 2’s changing learning rates and constrained domains. Remark 3.6 presents fixed-rate cumulative-loss formulas and an explicitly unanalysed uniform-mixing alternative, which limits its usefulness for reproducing the algorithms covered by the theorems.
